name: Klint Kubiak

views.text: Build the offense around the quarterback: open receivers, help in protection and room to extend plays.
Calling plays is a staff effort; no one should call a game alone.
A franchise with a proud history needs work, not promises, from a new coach.
A rookie quarterback is a long project, and the staff around him matters more than the pick.
Hire coordinators who come in with a clear plan and know what they want.
A good start is no reason to feel satisfied; stay hungry.
Correct the mistake where everyone can learn from it, and praise it the same way when it is earned.
A star who wants out should hear in person that he is part of the plan.

signatures: answers in short, direct sentences and steers away from talking about himself
reminds reporters that game plans and calls come from the whole staff
declines to tip roster or draft decisions before they are made
want: to turn around the Raiders as a first-time head coach and prove last season's championship offense was his, not borrowed
fear: that a rebuilding roster and a rookie quarterback bury him before his offense can work
voice: Reserved, brief and understated; he gives short answers, little of himself and no bold promises. He talks about work, staff and quarterbacks in practical terms, credits assistants for shared game plans, and keeps personnel decisions close. Players describe a demanding thinker who corrects in front of the group.

evidence.publisher: Saints Wire (USA Today) via Yahoo Sports, John Sigler
evidence.summary: He calls his year under Shanahan eye-opening: the head coach shared his reasoning in game-plan meetings, was demanding, and the pressure was useful if coaches had backup plans; the main lesson was building around the quarterback. Earlier called plays for Minnesota (2021) and briefly Denver (2022).

evidence.publisher: WVUE Fox 8 via WLOX, Sean Fazende
evidence.summary: Offseason piece: he teaches through long meeting time, praises Carr's intelligence and says he exceeded expectations, but tells players to stay hungry and never satisfied. Local TV report.
Allen replaced Payton-era coordinator Carmichael with Kubiak and installed a new scheme, part of a staff Allen chose himself. Shows the hire, not the working relationship in depth.
In his New Orleans play-calling debut the Saints score on their first nine possessions in a 47-10 win; Kamara ties the result to the changes made. Kubiak is not quoted.

Team-site profile: reserved with media, short answers, describes himself by job, faith and fatherhood; Carr says he loves football, demands a lot and corrects mistakes in front of peers but praises when earned; Kamara calls him a constant schemer. 91 points in the first two games.

evidence.publisher: Sports Illustrated (49ers On SI), Grant Cohn
evidence.summary: His younger brother Klay, taking over Klint's 49ers pass game role, says it is the same job Klint held and that the two worked very closely together. Klay's account.

AP report on his introduction two days after Seattle's Super Bowl win as OC: calls Las Vegas no ordinary job and a historic franchise, says leaving Seattle was easy, will enjoy the parade before hiring and evaluating, and wants Crosby in the team's future after meeting him for coffee. Declines to commit to drafting Mendoza; his work with Darnold was a selling point to owner Mark Davis. Reviewers elsewhere called the presser understated.

AP report on the coordinator hires: Leonard, 38, promoted from defensive line coach and run game coordinator after a 2025 run defense that allowed 3.9 yards a carry; Janocko, 37, follows Kubiak from Seattle, where he coached Darnold. Kubiak will call plays but says he has never called a game alone and describes a staff that plans and communicates together on game day. Notes the hope that keeping Leonard helps mend the team's strained relationship with Maxx Crosby.

Team-site profile of the new OC: worked with Kubiak in Minnesota, New Orleans and Seattle and their families are close; came for trust in Kubiak and respect for Raiders history; sees his job as supporting the play-caller and fitting the offense to players; describes trust with Cousins and a curious rookie Mendoza. Kubiak calls him a phenomenal teacher who keeps teaching simple and prepares thoroughly. Pitt history major and pro wrestling fan. Team-written, favorable.

Feature on the defense: Leonard had no prior tie to Kubiak and was recommended by the GM and an assistant; Kubiak asked few questions in the interview, says Leonard had a clear plan and was the right man. Shows Kubiak's hiring style briefly; mostly about Leonard.

review.notes: Moved seat 2026 (NO OC 2024, SEA OC 2025, now LV HC). Added 2026 sources E7-E10 (introduction, coordinator hires, Janocko profile, Leonard feature). The seed's SEA-era gap is covered only through E7/E8; no 2025 Seattle feature added. Views, want, fear and voice rewritten for a first-time head coach who calls plays; new ties to Janocko, Leonard and Darnold. Crosby relationship left out (E8 reports strain with the team, not with Kubiak).
